top_choice_rationale: P001 rewards a rare case in which a parameter-free continuum model (Bistritzer and MacDonald, 2011) predicted a qualitatively new regime, flat bands at a magic twist angle, and experiment (Jarillo-Herrero and collaborators, 2018) then delivered gate-tunable correlated insulators and superconductivity in a carbon-only system, since reproduced by many groups and extended to other moire platforms. The platform and phases are secure; the unresolved pairing mechanism bears on citation wording, not on validity. The three-name allocation keeps Bistritzer, first author of the joint prediction, and pairs prediction with the decisive experimental programme. The omission of Cao, Fatemi and others is a real gap that the citation should state openly, without claiming to settle priority or explain pairing. P002 (optical lattice clock, Katori and Ye) is a strong, more finished, cleanly credited second choice, but I weight novelty of the regime opened first and completeness of confirmation second. No award ranks last because both proposals are sound achievements.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; my electronic-structure and magnetism research is adjacent to moire flat-band physics, but I have no documented tie to any credited name in P001 or P002
